THE QUICK START

Getting started

Use NGHTML control-flow templates inside Lit-powered Web Components.

01 / INSTALL

Install the packages

Install NGHTML as a development dependency. Lit is a peer dependency and should be installed in your app as well. 

npm install lit
npm install -D @kurama-labs/nghtml

NGHTML is used in your app's Lit templates and compiled by your existing frontend bundler.

02 / IMPORT

Import nghtml

Import the template tag from the package root. Lit provides the custom-element lifecycle; NGHTML parses control flow and renders a Lit template. 

import { LitElement } from 'lit';
import { nghtml } from '@kurama-labs/nghtml';

interface Task {
  id: number;
  label: string;
}

class TaskList extends LitElement {
  static properties = {
    tasks: { type: Array },
  };

  tasks: Task[] = [
    { id: 1, label: 'Explore NGHTML' },
    { id: 2, label: 'Build a web component' },
  ];

  render() {
    return nghtml`
      <ul>
        @for (task of ${this.tasks}; track task.id) {
          <li>{{ task.label }}</li>
        } @empty {
          <li>No tasks yet.</li>
        }
      </ul>
      @if (${this.tasks.length > 0}) {
        <p>You have tasks to do.</p>
      } @else {
        <p>Add your first task to get started.</p>
      }
    `;
  }
}

customElements.define('task-list', TaskList);

Use <task-list></task-list> in your HTML. NGHTML exports nghtml, NghtmlSyntaxError, and the NghtmlTemplate type from its package entry point.

03 / CONTROL FLOW

Template syntax

@if / @else

Render conditional branches and optional aliases.

@for / @empty

Render iterable values with a required tracking expression.

@switch

Choose matching @case blocks with an optional default.

@let

Bind a value for use in subsequent template scope.

Supply JavaScript values with ${value}, then read loop and alias values with {{ task.label }}. Lit @click=${handler} events and supported [class.*], [style.*], and [attr.*] bindings work alongside the control flow. Invalid control-flow templates throw NghtmlSyntaxError.
